newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market ended higher on Thursday, after tame February CPI boosted expectations for a rate cut at Friday's Bank of Spain repo auction, dealers said.
February CPI fell 0.1 percent from January to grow 2.5 percent year-on-year versus 2.9 percent one month ago.
After the lower-than-expected inflation rate, a Reuter poll showed that a majority of financial experts expect a 25 basis point rate cut at tomorrow's repurchase agreement auction.
A rebounding Italian market also supported bonos. The 10-year spread over Bunds shrunk to around 127 bps.
Spain's yield curve steepened in reaction to the increased probability of a rate cut. The two- to 10-year spread rose to 129 basis points from 119 basis points at the close Wednesday.
The peseta remained weak, trading at around 84.84/88 per mark. The weakness could convince the Bank of Spain to be more cautious when considering a rate cut, analysts said.
